paragraphs: We are an internally managed real estate company that acquires, owns, and manages a diversified portfolio of single-tenant commercial retail properties, subject to long-term net leases with high-credit-quality tenants across the United States. We also invest in property developments and mortgage loans secured by real estate. As of December 31, 2025, we owned or had investments in 761 properties diversified by tenant, industry, and geography, comprising 129 different tenants across 28 retail sectors in 45 states. This includes three property developments where rent has not yet commenced. We focus on tenants in industries where we believe a physical location is critical to the generation of sales and profits, with a focus on necessity goods and essential services in the retail sector, including grocers, convenience stores, discount stores, home improvement, quick-service restaurants, general retail, and auto parts, all of which we refer to as defensive retail industries. As of December 31, 2025, our investments generated ABR1 of $198.3 million. Approximately 44% of our ABR is from investment grade2 credit rated tenants and an additional 14% of our ABR is derived from tenants with an investment grade profile3. Our portfolio was 99.9% occupied and, excluding mortgage loans receivable, had a weighted average remaining lease term ("WALT") of 10.1 years.

We were formed as a Maryland corporation on October 11, 2019, and our common stock began trading on the New York Stock Exchange ("NYSE") under the symbol "NTST" on August 13, 2020. We are structured as an umbrella partnership real estate investment trust (a "REIT"), meaning that we own our properties and conduct our business through our operating partnership, directly or through limited partnerships, limited liability companies or other subsidiaries. NETSTREIT GP, LLC, a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company, is the sole general partner of our operating partnership. As of December 31, 2025, we owned 99.6% of the units of limited partnership interests in our operating partnership ("OP Units"). We have elected to be treated and qualify as a REIT for U.S. federal income tax purposes.
The following highlights our significant transactions for the year ended December 31, 2025:
•We acquired 140 properties located in 31 states with a WALT of approximately 13.9 years for a total purchase price of $603.0 million, inclusive of $7.0 million of capitalized acquisition costs.
•We sold 78 properties, including one property under development, for a total sales price, net of disposal costs, of $169.1 million, recognizing a net gain of $7.7 million.

•In September 2025, we entered into a term loan agreement that provides for (i) a $200.0 million senior unsecured term loan that was fully funded at closing and matures in March 2031 (the "2031 Term Loan"), and (ii) a $250.0 million senior unsecured term loan that matures in September 2032, of which $100.0 million was funded at closing and $50.0 million was funded in January 2026 (the "2032 Term Loan").
1 Annualized base rent ("ABR") is annualized base rent for all leases that commenced and annualized cash interest on all executed mortgage loans as of December 31, 2025.

2 We define "investment grade" tenants as tenants, or tenants that are subsidiaries of a parent entity, with a credit rating of BBB- (S&P/Fitch), Baa3 (Moody's) or NAIC2 (National Association of Insurance Commissioners) or higher.

3 We define "investment grade profile" tenants as tenants with investment grade credit metrics (more than $1.0 billion in annual sales and a debt to adjusted EBITDA ratio of less than 2.0x), but do not carry a published rating from S&P, Moody's, or NAIC.

•In July 2025, we completed a registered public offering of 12,420,000 shares of our common stock on a forward basis at a public offering price of $17.70 per share, including the full exercise of the underwriters' option to purchase additional shares. We physically settled 8,155,053 of these shares in December 2025 and received $137.0 million of net proceeds.

•We entered into forward sale agreements with respect to an aggregate 9,068,486 shares of common stock under our existing $300.0 million at-the-market equity program established in August 2024 (the "2024 ATM Program") at a weighted-average price of $17.75 per share.

•In January 2025, we amended our existing credit agreements to provide for an aggregate of $550.0 million in senior unsecured term loans and to upsize our senior unsecured revolving credit facility to $500.0 million.

Our objective is to maximize stockholder value by generating attractive risk-adjusted returns through owning, managing, investing in, and growing a diversified portfolio of commercially desirable properties. As we continue to grow our portfolio, we seek to acquire single-tenant, commercial retail properties net leased on a long-term basis (generally at least ten years) to high credit quality tenants in industries where we believe a physical location is critical to the generation of sales and profits, with a focus on necessity goods and essential services in the retail sector, including grocers, convenience stores, discount stores, home improvement, quick-service restaurants, general retail, and auto parts. We believe these characteristics make our tenants' businesses e-commerce resistant and resilient through all economic cycles. Our current strategy targets a portfolio that, over time, will:

•derive no more than (i) 5% of its ABR from any single tenant or property, (ii) 15% of its ABR from any single retail sector, (iii) 15% of its ABR from any single state and (iv) 50% of its ABR from its top 10 tenants;

headings: Risks Related to Our Business and Properties
Global market and economic conditions may materially and adversely affect us and our tenants.
We are subject to risks related to commercial real estate ownership that could reduce the value of our properties.
We may not be able to successfully execute our acquisition or development strategies.
Our business is dependent upon our tenants successfully operating their businesses and their failure to do so could materially and adversely affect us.
Single-tenant leases involve significant risks of tenant default.
Our assessment that certain businesses are e-commerce resistant and recession-resilient may prove to be incorrect.
The tools we use to determine the creditworthiness of our tenants may not be accurate.
Our portfolio has geographic market concentrations that make us especially susceptible to adverse developments in those geographic markets.
We are subject to risks related to tenant concentration, and an adverse development with respect to a large tenant could materially and adversely affect us.
We may be unable to renew leases, lease vacant space, or re-lease space as leases expire on favorable terms or at all.
Defaults by borrowers on loans we originate could lead to losses.

Some of our tenants operate under franchise or license agreements, which, if terminated or not renewed prior to the expiration of their leases with us, would likely impair their ability to pay us rent.
The bankruptcy or insolvency of any of our tenants could result in the termination of such tenant's lease and material losses to us.
Illiquidity of real estate investments could significantly impede our ability to respond to adverse changes in the performance of our properties and harm our financial condition.
A loss of key management personnel could adversely affect our performance.

Any material failure, weakness, interruption, or breach in security of our information systems or data, or those of the third parties with whom we work, could prevent us from effectively operating our business.
Data privacy risks, including evolving laws, regulations, and other obligations and compliance efforts, may result in business interruption and increased costs and liabilities.
The use of artificial intelligence presents risks and challenges that may adversely impact our business and operating results or that of our tenants.
Insurance on our properties may not adequately cover losses, and uninsured losses could materially and adversely affect us.
We are subject to risks from natural disasters, such as hurricanes, tornados and flooding, and changes in weather patterns.
We may become subject to litigation, which could materially and adversely affect us.
We may acquire properties or portfolios of properties through tax deferred contribution transactions, which could result in stockholder dilution and limit our ability to sell such assets.

We may experience a decline in the fair value of our assets, which may have a material impact on our financial condition, liquidity, and results of operations and adversely impact the market price of our common stock.
The form, timing, and/or amount of dividend distributions in future periods may vary and be affected by economic and other considerations.
Risks Related to Financing our Business
Our growth depends on external sources of capital that are outside of our control and may not be available to us on commercially reasonable terms or at all.
Our level of indebtedness could materially and adversely affect our financial position, including reducing funds available for other business purposes and reducing our operational flexibility.
Failure to hedge effectively against interest rate changes may materially and adversely affect us.
Failure to maintain our current credit ratings could adversely affect our cost of funds, related margins, liquidity, and access to the debt capital markets.
Risks Related to Government Regulation and Tax Matters
If our operating partnership failed to qualify as a partnership or is not otherwise disregarded for U.S. federal income tax purposes, we would cease to qualify as a REIT.
Even if we qualify as a REIT for U.S. federal income tax purposes, we may be subject to other tax liabilities that reduce our cash flow and our ability to make distributions to stockholders.
paragraphs: Our operations and financial results are subject to various risks and uncertainties, including those described below. You should consider and read carefully all of the risks and uncertainties described below, together with all the other information contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including the section titled "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" and our consolidated financial statements and the related notes as well as other information filed with the SEC from time to time. The risks described below are those which we believe are the material risks we face. The occurrence of any of the following risks or additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently believe to be immaterial could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, or results of operations. In such case, the market price of our common stock could decline.

Changes in global or national market and economic conditions, such as global economic and financial market volatility and global geopolitical conflict, have caused, and may continue to cause, among other things, tightening in the credit markets, lower levels of liquidity, fluctuating interest rates and inflation, increases in the rate of default and bankruptcy, and lower consumer and business spending, which could materially and adversely affect us. For example, the recent macro-economic conditions of fluctuating interest and inflation rates have increased the costs associated with acquiring new properties and decreased the availability of financing on terms that we find attractive, which has reduced our ability to acquire properties at our historical rate with attractive terms. More recently, there have been significant changes to U.S. trade policies, treaties and tariffs, and ongoing discussion and commentary continue regarding potential further significant changes. This has created significant uncertainty about the future relationship between the United States and other countries with respect to trade policies, treaties and tariffs. These developments, or the perception that any of them could occur, may have a material adverse effect on global economic conditions and the stability of global financial markets, and may significantly reduce global trade and, in particular, trade between the impacted nations and the United States. Other potential consequences of changes in economic and financial conditions include, among others: changes in the performance of our tenants, which may result in lower rent and lower recoverable expenses than the tenant can afford to pay, and tenant defaults under their leases; current or potential tenants may delay or postpone entering into long-term leases with us; continuing increased costs of acquiring new properties on attractive terms; inability to borrow on terms and conditions that we find to be acceptable, which could continue to reduce our ability to pursue acquisition opportunities or increase future interest expense; and the recognition of impairment charges on or reduced values of our properties, which may adversely affect our results of operations or limit our ability to dispose of assets at attractive prices and may reduce the availability of buyer financing. We are also limited in our ability to reduce costs to offset the results of a prolonged or severe economic downturn given certain fixed costs and commitments associated with our operations, which we may be unable to renegotiate or offset. Accordingly, a decline in economic conditions could materially and adversely affect us.

Our core business is the ownership of single-tenant, commercial retail properties subject to long-term net leases across the United States. Accordingly, our performance is subject to risks incident to the ownership of commercial real estate, which include, among others, the inability to collect rents from tenants due to financial hardship, including bankruptcy; changes in local real estate conditions in the markets in which we operate, including the availability and demand for single-tenant, commercial retail properties space; changes in consumer trends and preferences that affect the demand for products and services offered by our tenants; inability to lease or sell properties upon expiration or termination of existing leases; environmental risks, including the presence of hazardous or toxic substances or materials on our properties; the subjectivity of real estate valuations and changes in these valuations over time; the illiquid nature of real estate compared to most other financial assets; changes in laws and governmental regulations, including those governing real estate usage and zoning; changes in interest rates and the availability of financing on attractive terms or at all; and changes in the general economic and business climate. The occurrence of any of these may cause the value of our real estate to decline, which could materially and adversely affect us.

Our ability to expand our portfolio through property acquisitions requires us to identify and complete acquisitions or investment opportunities on attractive terms that are compatible with our growth strategy and to successfully integrate newly acquired properties into our portfolio. The recent macro-economic conditions of fluctuating interest and inflation rates have increased the costs associated with acquiring new properties and decreased the availability of financing on terms that we find acceptable, which has reduced our ability to acquire properties at our historical rate with attractive terms. As a result, we may not be able to successfully implement our investment and acquisition strategies. We cannot assure you that our portfolio of properties will expand at all, or if it will expand at any specified rate or to any specified size. Because we may invest in markets other than the ones in which our current properties are located or properties which may be leased to tenants other than those to which we have historically leased properties, we may also be subject to the risks associated with investment in new markets or with new tenants that may be relatively unfamiliar to our management team.

Our property developments are subject to, without limitation, risks relating to the availability and timely receipt of zoning and other regulatory approvals and the cost and timely completion of construction (including risks from factors beyond our control, such as weather, labor conditions, or material shortages). Additionally, new development may involve risks related to construction delays or cost overruns that may increase anticipated project costs. These risks could result in substantial unanticipated delays or expenses and, under certain circumstances, could prevent completion of development activities once undertaken or provide a tenant with the opportunity to reduce rent or terminate a lease. Any of these situations may delay or eliminate proceeds or cash flows we expect from development projects, which could have an adverse effect on our financial condition.

Each of our properties is leased by a single tenant. Therefore, we believe that the success of our investments is materially dependent on the financial stability of our tenants. The success of any one of our tenants is dependent on the tenant's individual business and its industry, which could be adversely affected by poor management, global market and economic conditions in general, changes in consumer trends and preferences that decrease demand for a tenant's products or services, or other factors over which neither they nor we have control. Our portfolio includes properties leased to single tenants that operate in multiple locations, which means that, as of December 31, 2025, we owned numerous properties leased by the same entity (or related group of entities), including Dollar General, CVS, Walgreens, Family Dollar, Food Lion / Stop & Shop, Hobby Lobby, and Tractor Supply. To the extent we own numerous properties leased and/or operated by one entity (or related group of entities), the general failure of that single entity (or related group of entities) or a loss or significant decline in its business could materially and adversely affect us.

paragraphs: We are an internally managed real estate company that acquires, owns, and manages a diversified portfolio of single-tenant commercial retail properties, subject to long-term net leases with high-credit-quality tenants across the United States. We also invest in property developments and mortgage loans secured by real estate. As of December 31, 2025, we owned or had investments in 761 properties diversified by tenant, industry, and geography, comprising 129 different tenants across 28 retail sectors in 45 states. This includes three property developments where rent has not yet commenced. We focus on tenants in industries where we believe a physical location is critical to the generation of sales and profits, with a focus on necessity goods and essential services in the retail sector, including grocers, convenience stores, discount stores, home improvement, quick-service restaurants, general retail, and auto parts, all of which we refer to as defensive retail industries. As of December 31, 2025, our investments generated ABR1 of $198.3 million. Approximately 44% of our ABR is from investment grade2 credit rated tenants and an additional 14% of our ABR is derived from tenants with an investment grade profile3. Our portfolio was 99.9% occupied and, excluding mortgage loans receivable, had a weighted average remaining lease term ("WALT") of 10.1 years.

As a result of receiving an investment grade credit rating, the interest rate on our term loans and Revolver (as defined below), including our Revolver facility fee, is now determined by our credit rating and consolidated total leverage ratio. For the 2028 Term Loan, 2029 Term Loan, 2030 Term Loan A, 2030 Term Loan B, and 2031 Term Loan (each as defined below), our applicable margin was reduced by 20 basis points from 1.15% to 0.95%. For the 2032 Term Loan (as defined below), our applicable margin was reduced by 25 basis points from 1.50% to 1.25%. For the Revolver, our applicable margin was reduced by 15 basis points from 1.00% to 0.85%, and the facility fee increased by five basis points from 0.15% to 0.20%. See Note 6 – "Debt" for further discussion on our debt and interest rates.

On September 25, 2025, we entered into a Term Loan Agreement (the "PNC Term Loan Agreement") which provides for: a $200.0 million senior unsecured term loan (the "2031 Term Loan"), all of which was funded on the closing date, and a $250.0 million senior unsecured term loan (the "2032 Term Loan"), of which $100.0 million was funded on the closing date, $50.0 million was funded on January 2, 2026, and the remaining $100.0 million is available as a delayed draw term loan commitment until September 25, 2026. The 2031 Term Loan matures on March 25, 2031 and the 2032 Term Loan matures on September 24, 2032. We have fully hedged the 2031 Term Loan at an all-in fixed interest rate of 4.39% through March 2031. We have partially hedged $200.0 million of the 2032 Term Loan at an all-in fixed interest rate of 4.67% through September 2032, with the remaining $50.0 million of the 2032 Term Loan currently unhedged. Further, we amended our existing credit agreements agented by PNC Bank, National Association (the "PNC Credit Agreement"), Wells Fargo Bank, National Association (the "Wells Fargo Credit Agreement") and Truist Bank (the "Truist Credit Agreement"), implementing certain conforming changes including, without limitation, removing the SOFR credit spread adjustments in those agreements.

In July 2025, we completed a registered public offering of 12,420,000 shares of our common stock at a public offering price of $17.70 per share, including the full exercise of the underwriters' option to purchase additional shares. In connection with the offering, we entered into forward sale agreements for 12,420,000 shares of our common stock. We did not initially receive any proceeds from the sale of shares of common stock by the forward purchasers.

On December 30, 2025, we physically settled 8,155,053 shares of common stock at a weighted-average price of $16.81 per share in accordance with the forward sale agreements. We received net proceeds from the settlement of $137.0 million, net of underwriting discounts and offering costs of $7.6 million. As of December 31, 2025, 4,264,947 shares remain unsettled under the July 2025 forward sale agreements. We expect to physically settle the forward sale agreements (by delivery of shares of common stock) and receive proceeds from the sale of those shares upon one or more forward settlement dates, which shall occur no later than July 28, 2026.
1 Annualized base rent ("ABR") is annualized base rent for all leases that commenced and annualized cash interest for all executed mortgage loans as of December 31, 2025.

2 We define "investment grade" tenants as tenants, or tenants that are subsidiaries of a parent entity, with a credit rating of BBB- (S&P/Fitch), Baa3 (Moody's) or NAIC2 (National Association of Insurance Commissioners) or higher.

3 We define "investment grade profile" tenants as tenants with investment grade credit metrics (more than $1.0 billion in annual sales and a debt to adjusted EBITDA ratio of less than 2.0x), but do not carry a published rating from S&P, Moody's, or NAIC.

During 2025, we entered into forward sale agreements with respect to an aggregate 9,068,486 shares of common stock under the existing $300.0 million at-the-market equity program established in August 2024 (the "2024 ATM Program") at a weighted-average price of $17.75 per share.

paragraphs: 本公司為 internally managed 的不動產公司，主要從事取得、擁有及管理美國各州多樣化的單租戶商業零售不動產，並與高信用等級租戶簽訂長期淨租約。本公司亦投資於不動產開發案及以不動產為擔保的房貸貸款。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司擁有或投資於 761 個不動產，分散於租戶、產業及地理區域，包含 129 家不同租戶，分佈於 28 個零售產業，遍及 45 個州。此包含三個不動產開發案，其租金尚未開始。本公司專注於產業中認為實體據點對銷售及獲利至關重要的租戶，特別是零售產業中必需品及基本服務，包括雜貨店、便利商店、折扣商店、傢俱裝修、速食餐廳、一般零售及汽車零件，本公司將這些產業稱為防禦性零售產業。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司投資產生的 ABR 為 198.3 百萬美元。約 44% 的 ABR 來自投資等級信用評等租戶，另有 14% 的 ABR 來自具有投資等級評估的租戶。本公司資產佔用率為 99.9%，扣除房貸貸款應收款後，加權平均剩餘租約期間（"WALT"）為 10.1 年。

本公司於 2019 年 10 月 11 日在馬裏蘭州成立為公司，並於 2020 年 8 月 13 日在紐約證券交易所（"NYSE"）以 "NTST" 為代碼開始交易。本公司為一傘型合夥不動產投資信託（"REIT"），表示本公司擁有不動產並透過經營合夥公司進行業務，直接或透過有限合夥、有限責任公司或其他子公司。NETSTREIT GP, LLC，為本公司之 wholly-owned subsidiary，為本公司經營合夥公司的唯一普通合夥人。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司持有經營合夥公司（"OP Units"）有限合夥權益單位的 99.6%。本公司已選擇並符合美國聯邦所得稅法規之 REIT 規定。
以下為本公司 2025 年 12 月 31 日財務年度重大交易之重點：
•本公司取得 140 個不動產，位於 31 個州，加權平均剩餘租約期間（"WALT"）約為 13.9 年，總購置價格為 603.0 百萬美元，包含 7.0 百萬美元之取得成本資本化。
•本公司出售 78 個不動產，包含一個開發中不動產，總銷售價格扣除處分成本為 169.1 百萬美元，確認淨獲利 7.7 百萬美元。

•2025 年 9 月，本公司與電信業者簽訂定期貸款協議，提供 (i) 200.0 百萬美元之無擔保高級定期貸款，於交易時已完全融資，並於 2031 年 3 月到期（"2031 年定期貸款"），以及 (ii) 250.0 百萬美元之無擔保高級定期貸款，於 2032 年 9 月到期，其中 100.0 百萬美元於交易時已融資，50.0 百萬美元於 2026 年 1 月融資（"2032 年定期貸款"）。
1 年度基本租金（"ABR"）為截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日所有已開始租約之年度基本租金，以及所有已簽訂房貸貸款之年度現金利息。
2 我們將 "投資等級" 租戶定義為租戶或為母公司之子公司，其信用評等為 BBB-（S&P/Fitch）、Baa3（Moody's）或 NAIC2（國家保險委員會）或更高。
3 我們將「投資等級資產」租戶定義為具有投資等級信用指標（年營收超過 1.0 十億美元，且負債與調整後 EBITDA 比率低於 2.0 倍）的租戶，但並未取得 S&P、Moody's 或 NAIC 發佈的評級。
•2025 年 7 月，我們完成一筆註冊公開發行，發行 12,420,000 股普通股，以每股 17.70 美元的公開發行價格，包含經理人行使選擇權購買額外股份的全部行使，我們於 2025 年 12 月實際交付 8,155,053 股，並收到 137.0 百萬美元的淨資金。
•我們與電信業者簽訂遠期銷售協議，就我們現有於2024年8月建立的、總額為300.0百萬美元的市場價股權計劃（稱為"2024 ATM 程式"）下合計9,068,486股普通股，以加權平均每股17.75美元價格進行交易。

我們的目標是透過擁有、管理、投資並成長一個多元化的商業上具吸引力的不動產組合，以最大化股東價值。隨著我們持續擴充組合，我們致力於取得單一租戶、商業零售不動產，以長期租賃方式（通常至少為十年）出租給高信用等級租戶，這些租戶所屬產業我們認為實體門店對銷售與獲利至關重要，重點在零售業中必需商品與基本服務，包括雜貨店、便利商店、折扣商店、傢俱裝修、速食餐廳、一般零售與汽車零件。我們認為這些特質使我們租戶的業務對網路購物具有抗性，並在所有經濟週期中表現堅韌。我們目前的策略目標是建立一個組合，隨著時間的推移，將：
•來自任何單一租戶或不動產的 ABR 不超過 (i) 5%，(ii) 來自任何單一零售業的 ABR 不超過 15%，(iii) 來自任何單一州的 ABR 不超過 15%，以及 (iv) 來自前 10 大租戶的 ABR 不超過 50%。

paragraphs: 本公司為 internally managed 的不動產公司，從事取得、擁有及管理多樣化的單租戶商業零售不動產組合，這些不動產以美國境內長期淨租賃方式出租給信用品質高的租戶。本公司亦投資於不動產開發案及以不動產為擔保的房貸。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司擁有或投資於 761 個不動產，這些不動產依租戶、產業及地理區域分散，包含 129 家不同租戶，分佈於 28 個零售產業，遍及 45 個州。此包含三個不動產開發案，其租金尚未開始。本公司著重於產業中認為實體據點對銷售及獲利至關重要的租戶，重點在零售產業中必需品及基本服務，包括雜貨店、便利商店、折扣商店、傢俱裝修、速食餐廳、一般零售及汽車零件，本公司將這些產業稱為防禦性零售產業。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司投資產生的 ABR 為 198.3 百萬美元。約 44% 的 ABR 來自投資等級信用評等的租戶，另外 14% 的 ABR 來自具有投資等級評估特質的租戶。本公司資產組合的佔用率為 99.9%，扣除房貸應收款後，加權平均剩餘租賃期間（"WALT"）為 10.1 年。

因取得投資等級信用評等，本公司.term loans 及 Revolver（如下所定）的利率現已根據本公司信用評等及合併總負債對營收比率決定。對於 2028 年期貸款、2029 年期貸款、2030 年期貸款 A、2030 年期貸款 B 及 2031 年期貸款（如下所定），適用利率減少了 20 基點，由 1.15% 降至 0.95%。對於 2032 年期貸款（如下所定），適用利率減少了 25 基點，由 1.50% 降至 1.25%。對於 Revolver，適用利率減少了 15 基點，由 1.00% 降至 0.85%，且場地費用增加了 5 基點，由 0.15% 升至 0.20%。有關本公司債務及利率的進一步討論，請參閱附註 6 – "債務"。

2025 年 9 月 25 日，本公司與 PNC Bank, National Association（"PNC Credit Agreement"）簽訂了期貸款協議（"PNC 期貸款協議"），該協議提供：2031 年期貸款（"2031 年期貸款"）為 200.0 百萬美元的高級無擔保期貸款（"2031 年期貸款"），全部貸款於簽約日完成；以及 2032 年期貸款（"2032 年期貸款"）為 250.0 百萬美元的高級無擔保期貸款，其中 100.0 百萬美元於簽約日完成，50.0 百萬美元於 2026 年 1 月 2 日完成，剩餘 100.0 百萬美元為延後提款期貸款承諾，至 2026 年 9 月 25 日為止。2031 年期貸款於 2031 年 3 月 25 日到期，2032 年期貸款於 2032 年 9 月 24 日到期。本公司已完全對 2031 年期貸款進行利率對沖，利率為 4.39%，至 2031 年 3 月。本公司已部分對沖 2032 年期貸款中的 200.0 百萬美元，利率為 4.67%，至 2032 年 9 月，剩餘 50.0 百萬美元的 2032 年期貸款目前尚未對沖。此外，本公司修改了現有信用協議，由 PNC Bank, National Association（"PNC Credit Agreement"）、Wells Fargo Bank, National Association（"Wells Fargo Credit Agreement"）及 Truist Bank（"Truist Credit Agreement"）代理，實施某些符合規定的變更，包括但不限於移除這些協議中的 SOFR 信用利差調整。
2025 年 7 月，本公司完成註冊公開發行 12,420,000 股普通股，發行價格為每股 17.70 美元，包括經發行機構行使選擇權後購買額外股份的全部數量。為配合此次發行，本公司與 12,420,000 股普通股的遠期銷售協議。本公司在遠期買方出售股份時，並未 initially 收到任何資金。

2025 年 12 月 30 日，本公司根據遠期銷售協議，實際交付 8,155,053 股普通股，加權平均價格為每股 16.81 美元。本公司從此交易中收到淨資金 137.0 百萬美元，扣除經紀折扣及發行費用 7.6 百萬美元。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，根據 2025 年 7 月遠期銷售協議，尚有 4,264,947 股未交付。本公司預期於一個或多個遠期結算日，實際交付這些股份並收到銷售資金，這些結算日將不遲於 2026 年 7 月 28 日。
1 年度基本租金（"ABR"）為截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，所有已開始的租賃的年度基本租金，以及所有已執行的房貸的年度現金利息。
2 我們將 "投資等級" 租戶定義為租戶，或為母公司之子公司，其信用評等為 BBB-（S&P/Fitch）、Baa3（Moody's）或 NAIC2（國家保險委員會）或更高。
3 我們將「投資等級資格租戶」定義為具有投資等級信用指標的租戶（年度銷售額超過 1.0 十億美元，且負債與調整後 EBITDA 比率低於 2.0 倍），但未取得 S&P、Moody's 或 NAIC 發布的評級。
於 2025 年，本公司與電信業者簽訂遠期銷售協議，就現有 300.0 百萬美元於市場價格發行股票計畫（於 2024 年 8 月建立，稱為 "2024 ATM 程式"）下合計 9,068,486 股普通股，平均價格為每股 17.75 美元。

本公司之資產組合具有地理市場集中性，使其尤其容易受到該地理市場不利發展之影響。
本公司面臨與租戶集中度相關之風險，且對大型租戶之不利發展可能對本公司造成重大且不利之影響。
本公司可能無法在租約到期時以有利條件續約、出租空置空間或重新出租空間。
我們所發放之貸款借款人違約，可能導致我們產生虧損。
部分租戶係以特許經營或授權契約方式營運，若其在租約到期前未續約或終止契約，將可能影響其支付我們租金之能力。
任一租戶之破產或財務困難，可能導致該租戶租約終止，並對本公司造成重大虧損。
不動產投資之流動性不足，可能顯著阻礙本公司對不動產績效不利變動之應對，並損害本公司財務狀況。
關鍵管理人員之流失可能對本公司之績效造成不利影響。
任何重大系統或資料之功能失常、弱點、中斷或安全漏洞，可能導致本公司無法有效運作業務。
資料隱私風險，包括不斷演進的法律、法規及其他義務與合規努力，可能導致業務中斷與成本及負債增加。
人工智慧之使用可能帶來風險與挑戰，可能對本公司或租戶之業務與營運成果產生不利影響。
本公司財產之保險可能無法充分覆蓋損失，未保險之損失可能對本公司造成重大且不利影響。
本公司可能面臨天然災害，如颶風、龍捲風及水災，以及氣候模式變動之風險。
本公司可能遭提起訴訟，可能對本公司造成重大且不利影響。
本公司可能透過延稅之方式取得財產或財產組合，可能導致股東稀釋，並限制本公司出售該等資產之能力。
本公司可能面臨資產公允價值下跌，可能對財務狀況、流動性及營運成果產生重大影響，並對本公司普通股之市場價格產生不利影響。
未來各期間的股息發放形式、時機與/或金額可能有所變動，並可能受經濟及其他因素的影響。
與籌資業務相關的風險
本公司之成長取決於外部資金來源，而這些資金來源並非本公司所能控制，且可能無法以商業上合理之條件或完全無法取得。
本公司之負債水平可能對本公司之財務狀況產生重大且不利的影響，包括減少用於其他業務用途之資金，以及降低本公司之營運彈性。
若未能有效對應利率變動進行避險，可能對本公司產生重大且不利的影響。
若未能維持現有信用評級，可能對本公司之資金成本、相關毛利率、流動性及取得債務資本市場之能力產生不利影響。
與政府規範及稅務事項相關的風險
若本公司之營運合夥企業未能符合合夥企業之資格，或未被美國聯邦所得稅用途所忽略，則本公司將無法符合REIT之資格。

paragraphs: 本公司之營運及財務表現受多種風險與不確定性影響，包括下文所述者。請考慮並仔細閱讀下文所述之所有風險與不確定性，並與本年度10-K表報表中所包含之所有資訊一併審閱，包括標題為「管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之討論與分析」之部分，以及我們之合併財務報表與相關附註，以及其他時而向SEC提交之資訊。下文所述之風險為本公司認為對我們而言為重要之風險。任何下列風險或尚未為本公司所知之其他風險與不確定性，或本公司目前認為為次要之風險，均可能對本公司之營運、財務狀況或營運結果造成重大且不利之影響。在此情況下，本公司普通股之市場價格可能下跌。

全球或國家市場與經濟條件之變動，例如全球經濟與金融市場之波動及全球地緣政治衝突，已導致，且可能繼續導致，諸如信用市場緊縮、流動性水準降低、利率與通貨膨脹波動、違約與破產率增加，以及消費者與企業支出減少等情況，這可能對本公司造成重大且不利之影響。例如，近期總體經濟條件中利率與通貨膨脹率之波動，已增加取得新不動產之相關成本，並降低以本公司認為具有吸引力之條件取得融資之可得性，這已降低本公司以歷史速度以具吸引力之條件取得不動產之能力。更近期來，美國貿易政策、條約與關稅已出現重大變動，且持續有討論與評論關於潛在進一步重大變動。這已造成美國與其他國家之間就貿易政策、條約與關稅之未來關係產生重大不確定性。這些發展，或對任何這些發展之看法，可能對全球經濟條件與全球金融市場之穩定造成重大影響，並可能顯著減少全球貿易，特別是受影響國家與美國之間之貿易。經濟與金融條件變動之其他潛在後果包括，例如：租戶之營運表現變動，這可能導致租金與租戶無法負擔之可回收費用減少，以及租戶在其租賃契約下之違約；現有或潛在租戶可能延後或擱置與本公司簽訂長期租賃契約；持續增加以具吸引力條件取得新不動產之成本；無法以本公司認為可接受之條件取得貸款，這可能持續降低本公司追求取得機會之能力或增加未來利息支出；以及對不動產之減值費用認列或不動產價值降低，這可能對本公司營運結果造成不利影響或限制本公司以具吸引力價格處置資產之能力，並可能降低買方融資之可得性。我們在面對延長或嚴重經濟衰退時，受限於某些固定成本與承諾，這些成本與承諾與本公司營運相關，而我們可能無法重新協議或抵銷。因此，經濟條件之下降可能對本公司造成重大且不利之影響。

本公司核心業務為擁有美國境內之單一租戶商業零售不動產，並簽訂長期淨租賃契約。因此，本公司之表現受商業不動產所有權相關風險影響，包括，例如：因租戶財務困難（包括破產）而無法收取租金；本公司營運之市場中之地方不動產條件變動，包括單一租戶商業零售不動產之可得性與需求；消費者趨勢與偏好變動，這會影響租戶所提供產品與服務之需求；無法在現有租賃契約到期或終止時出租或出售不動產；環境風險，包括本公司不動產上存在有害或有毒物質或材料；不動產評價之主觀性與這些評價隨時間之變動；與大多數其他金融資產相比，不動產之流動性較低；法律與政府法規變動，包括那些規範不動產使用與 zoning（土地使用分區）之法規；利率變動與以具吸引力條件或任何條件取得融資之可得性變動；以及總體經濟與商業氣候之變動。任何上述情況之發生，可能導致本公司不動產價值下降，這可能對本公司造成重大且不利之影響。

本公司透過取得不動產以擴充資產組合之能力，需識別並完成符合本公司成長策略之取得或投資機會，且成功整合新取得之不動產至資產組閤中。近期總體經濟條件中利率與通貨膨脹率之波動，已增加取得新不動產之相關成本，並降低以本公司認為具有吸引力之條件取得融資之可得性，這已降低本公司以歷史速度以具吸引力之條件取得不動產之能力。因此，本公司可能無法成功實施投資與取得策略。本公司無法保證本公司之不動產資產組合將擴張，或若擴張，則擴張速度或規模是否符合特定標準。由於本公司可能投資於目前不動產所在地以外之市場，或投資於租賃給與本公司歷史租賃租戶不同之租戶之不動產，本公司亦可能面臨投資新市場或與新租戶相關之風險，而這些租戶對本公司管理團隊而言可能較為陌生。

本公司之不動產開發受多種風險影響，包括但不限於取得 zoning（土地使用分區）及其他法規許可之可得性與及時取得，以及建設之成本與及時完成（包括因超出本公司控制範圍之因素，例如天氣、勞工條件或材料短缺等所產生之風險）。此外，新開發可能涉及建設延誤或成本超支，這可能增加預期之項目成本。這些風險可能導致重大且未預期之延誤或費用，並在某些情況下，可能導致開發活動無法完成，或提供租戶減少租金或終止租賃契約之機會。任何上述情況可能延誤或消除本公司預期自開發項目所得之資金流入，這可能對本公司財務狀況造成不利影響。

本公司每一處不動產均由單一租戶租賃。因此，本公司認為本公司投資之成功在很大程度上依賴租戶之財務穩定性。任何單一租戶之成功取決於該租戶之個別業務及其產業，這可能因管理不善、總體市場與經濟條件、消費者趨勢與偏好變動而降低對租戶產品或服務之需求，或其他本公司與租戶均無法控制之因素而受到不利影響。本公司之資產組合包含由單一租戶租賃之不動產，這些租戶在多個地點營運，這意味著截至2025年12月31日，本公司擁有許多由同一實體（或相關實體羣組）租賃與/或營運之不動產，包括Dollar General、CVS、Walgreens、Family Dollar、Food Lion / Stop & Shop、Hobby Lobby，以及Tractor Supply。在本公司擁有許多由同一實體（或相關實體羣組）租賃與/或營運之不動產之情況下，該單一實體（或相關實體羣組）之普遍失敗或該實體（或相關實體羣組）之業務損失或顯著下降，可能對本公司造成重大且不利之影響。
